title: 06_reduction_supported runs &, |, ~&, ~| in an analog block and calls the LRM ban an extension
detail: VERIFIED. ch4-expressions.html 4.2.10 verbatim: "The reduction operators can not be used inside the analog block and only have meaning when used in the digital context." The fixture has no //! reject, so the contract requires it to compile, build a testbench and print ok=1 for four CHECKI wants on &bits, ~&bits, ~|bits inside `analog begin`. Its own header admits the conflict and calls it an extension. Sibling 07 rejects only `^`, so the suite currently asserts four of the five reduction operators are legal where the LRM bans all five. src/diag_code.zig has E0319 ("reduction operator requires an integer operand", 4.2.10) and E0320 ("xor reduction is not in the analog subset", lrm C) but NO code for the analog-block ban itself, so a new code is required.
expected: //! reject <new code for the 4.2.10 analog-block ban>\n//! lrm 4.2.10\n//! xfail VerA accepts &, |, ~& and ~| inside the analog block. Delete the CHECKI wants; a rejected file runs nothing. Rename to 06_reduction_rejected.va so 06 and 07 read as one rule.

title: 86_same_flow_terminals contributes I(p,p) and pins V(p,p)==0.0; Table 4-16 lists both as Error
detail: VERIFIED against docs/VAMS-LRM/ch4-expressions.html: Table 4-16 contains the rows `V(n1,n1) Error` and `I(n1,n1) Error`, and the prose under it repeats the rule twice ("If two net expressions are given as arguments to a flow access function, they shall not evaluate to the same signal"). The fixture has no //! reject, contains `I(p,p) <+ 1m;` and CHECKX("V(p,p) = 0", V(p,p), 0.0). Its header claim ("a branch from p to p has a potential of exactly zero") is arithmetic, not LRM. The 0.0 want is over-specification, not a wrong number. src/diag_code.zig E0315 already documents the exact ban in its explain text: "LRM 4.4 also forbids `V(n1, n1)`", so the code to demand exists.
expected: //! reject E0315\n//! lrm 4.4\n//! xfail VerA has no same-signal branch check. Drop both CHECKX lines. Keep the V(p)==0.7 want only if it is moved into 13_signal_access.va, where it is reachable.

title: 87_wrong_discipline_access is named for an illegal V(p) it never asserts, and the legal want it does assert is unreachable
detail: VERIFIED. 4.4: "The access function name shall match the discipline declaration for the nets, ports, or branch given in the argument expression list." `p` is ch4_custom_d, whose potential nature declares access=CustomV, so `V(p) <+ 0.0;` on line 31 is the violation the filename names. The file carries no //! reject, so the contract requires it to compile; its only assertion is CHECKR on the LEGAL CustomV(p)==0.7. That want is arithmetically correct (bias 0.7) but a conforming compiler rejects the file before reaching it. Two rules are entangled in one file. src/diag_code.zig E0501 ("unknown access function", lrm 3.6.1.4) is the code to demand.
expected: Split. 87_wrong_discipline_access.va becomes `//! reject E0501` + `//! lrm 4.4` + `//! xfail` with only the `V(p) <+ 0.0;` line and no CHECKs. Move the CustomV(p)==0.7 want to a new accept fixture 110_custom_discipline_access.va.

title: 99 is named for the 4.7.1 named-block ban and instead asserts what the banned construct computes
detail: VERIFIED. 4.7.1 bullet list, verbatim: an analog user-defined function "shall not use named blocks". The fixture writes `begin : forbidden` inside `analog function real named` and, with no //! reject, is required to compile and print ok=1 for CHECKX(named(0.75), 0.75). The header openly says "VerA has no diagnostic for the rule today ... so the fixture instead pins what the construct is required to produce IF it is accepted" - which inverts the suite's contract. No diag code exists for this bullet; one is needed.
expected: //! reject <new 4.7.1 named-block code>\n//! lrm 4.7.1\n//! xfail no diagnostic for the 4.7.1 bullet list yet. Drop the CHECKX.

title: 100 requires a zero-formal analog function to compile and run; 4.7.1 requires at least one formal
detail: VERIFIED. 4.7.1: an analog user-defined function "shall have at least one formal argument declared". `analog function real noargs;` has none and is called as `noargs()`. No //! reject, so it must compile and print ok=1 for CHECKX(noargs(), 1.0). The file's own NOTE concedes "a strict reading rejects this module rather than running it". Shares a new diag code with CH04-004/006.
expected: //! reject <new 4.7.1 formal-count code>\n//! lrm 4.7.1\n//! xfail. Drop the CHECKX and the `I(p) <+ noargs();` contribution.

title: 101 requires an undeclared formal to compile and run, and attributes to 4.7.1 a default it does not grant
detail: VERIFIED. 4.7.1: "all formal arguments shall have an associated block item declaration specifying the data type of the argument". The fixture declares `input x;` with no `real x;`. Separately, its header says "VerA applies the 4.7.1 default of real" - 4.7.1's "if unspecified, the default is real" governs the FUNCTION RETURN TYPE, not formals; there is no default for a formal's type. The 0.75 want is arithmetically fine and normatively unreachable.
expected: //! reject <new 4.7.1 formal-type code>\n//! lrm 4.7.1\n//! xfail. Drop the CHECKX and correct the header's misattribution of the `real` default.

title: 108 demands ParseError for an array assignment-pattern output actual that 4.7.2.3 mandates
detail: VERIFIED. The fixture is `//! reject ParseError` on `fill(V(p),'{a,b})`. 4.7.2.3/4.7.2.4 require exactly this form for array output/inout actuals, and 4.7.2.3's worked example is the LRM's own `dummy = arrayadd(x,'{y,z});`. A conforming compiler accepts the file and FAILS this fixture. This is an inverted reject: it locks the parser gap in as correct.
expected: Rewrite as a running fixture: `//! lrm 4.7.2.3` + `//! xfail VerA's parser has no array formals yet`, with CHECKX wants on a and b after the call (a==V(p), b==2.0*V(p) under a stated bias). Delete 108_function_array_output_pattern.expected-error.txt.

title: 109 demands ParseError for the LRM's own arrayadd worked example
detail: VERIFIED. `//! reject ParseError` on `bump('{a,b})`. 4.7.2.4 in ch4-expressions.html states the case in full and works the numbers: "x[0] = 5; x[1] = 10; y = 3; z = 6; dummy = arrayadd(x,'{y,z});" ... "will update the vector variable x with values x[0] = 8 and x[1] = 16". Those two integers are a free literal oracle a conforming compiler must produce.
expected: Rewrite as a running fixture reproducing the LRM's arrayadd example verbatim, with `//! lrm 4.7.2.4`, CHECKX(x[0],8.0) and CHECKX(x[1],16.0), plus `//! xfail` while array formals do not parse. Delete the sidecar.

title: 13b rejects potential()/flow(), which 4.4 explicitly supports, on the bare substring "expression"
detail: VERIFIED. 4.4, verbatim: "As an alternative to using the access attribute specified in the discipline, the generic potential and flow access functions are also supported (see 5.5.1)." Table 4-16 lists `potential(b1)` and `flow(n1)` as valid rows, and the general rule permits "a list of one or two nets or port expressions", so `potential(p,n)` and `flow(p,n)` are both legal. The fixture is `//! reject expression` - a substring so generic that almost any diagnostic satisfies it - on legal code.
expected: Rewrite as a running fixture 13b_generic_access.va: `//! lrm 4.4`, CHECKEQ that potential(p,n)==V(p,n) and flow(p,n)==I(p,n) (an identity with no digits, which is what CHECKEQ exists for), plus `//! xfail` while VerA lacks the generic names. Delete the sidecar.

title: 37_ac_stim demands GeneratedCompileError - a VerA codegen crash - for a call 4.6.3 defines and gives a DC value to
detail: VERIFIED. 4.6.3: "The AC stimulus function returns zero (0) during large-signal analyses (such as DC and transient)". The fixture is `//! reject GeneratedCompileError` on `ac_stim("ac", 1.0, 0.0)`. GeneratedCompileError is a harness phase label meaning the emitted Zig did not compile - the fixture pins a VerA crash as the expected behaviour of a normative function. COVERAGE.md line 43 admits it: "snapshots current generic-call behavior". 4.6.3 hands over the literal for free: under `//! analysis dc` the call is exactly 0.0.
expected: Rewrite as a running fixture: `//! analysis dc`, `//! lrm 4.6.3`, CHECKX("ac_stim returns zero in DC", ac_stim("ac",1.0,0.0), 0.0), plus `//! xfail` until codegen stops crashing. Delete the sidecar.

title: 31 rejects {4{2'b10}}, a form 4.2.13 permits and whose own example the section works out
detail: VERIFIED. The fixture's first line already says "DEBT - this rejection is NOT conformance. The LRM permits what VerA refuses here." 4.2.13 works the replication example itself: "result = {4{func(w)}} would be computed as: y = func(w); result = {y, y, y, y}". The fixture pins the parser message "expected `}`". Because it rejects, there is NO running replication anywhere in the chapter (30_concatenation.va has none), so all four of 4.2.13's replication rules are unexercised.
expected: Rewrite as a running fixture 31_replication.va: `//! lrm 4.2.13`, CHECKI("{4{2'b10}}", {4{2'b10}}, 170) (8 bits, 0b10101010), plus `//! xfail` naming the parser gap. Keep the ledger honest via xfail rather than an inverted reject. Delete the sidecar.

title: All four Z-filters are pinned to a DC output of 2.0, but 4.5.12 states no DC behaviour at all
detail: VERIFIED by reading 4.5.12 end to end: it specifies T ("shall be positive"), tau, t0, the null argument and each transfer function, and says NOTHING about DC or the operating point - unlike ddt (4.5.3), idt, absdelay, transition and slew, which each get an explicit DC sentence. The fixture derives 2.0 from H(z=1) of a one-pole accumulator, a defensible steady-state reading; but 4.5.15's "All analog operators are considered to have no state history prior to time t == 0" supports 1.0 just as well. The number is not WRONG, it is unearned - which is the more dangerous kind, because it looks derived.
expected: Keep the wants but replace the header's flat assertion with the reasoning and the alternative, and mark the fixture as pinning an implementation choice, not a normative value - or move it behind `//! xfail` pending a ruling. Do not silently keep 2.0 as if 4.5.12 said so.

title: The fourteen-term sum literal drops its last digit: 8.51602305493742 vs 8.516023054937422
detail: VERIFIED by recomputation in python3 at double precision, summing left-to-right in the fixture's own source order with x = 0.5*tanh(1.0) = 0.3807970779778824: the sum is 8.516023054937422. The fixture writes 8.51602305493742. Relative difference 2.1e-16, comfortably inside the fixture's own 1e-14 RTOL, so it passes today - and becomes a false failure the moment anyone tightens the tolerance, which is exactly what a reviewer checking digits would do.
expected: Change the want to 8.516023054937422.

title: The atan2-vs-atan identity is pinned at 1e-16, about 1.8 ulp of the value being differenced
detail: VERIFIED. atan(x) at x=0.3807970779778824 is 0.36373..., whose ulp is 5.55e-17, so the 1e-16 absolute tolerance on `atan2(x,1.0) - atan(x)` is 1.8 ulp. glibc happens to return exactly 0.0 today, so it passes, but nothing in Table 4-15 nor in C requires atan2(y,1) and atan(y) to agree bit-for-bit - they are separate library entry points. This is a tolerance that will fail on a different libm for a reason that is not a bug.
expected: Either relax to 1e-15 (about 18 ulp, still a real claim) or restate it with CHECKEQ, which is the macro README reserves for identities with no digits to write.

title: The $vt tolerance is 1e-4 where the Annex-D constant band it must admit is under 3e-5
detail: VERIFIED by computing kT/q at T=300.15 for all five Annex-D vintages: 0.025864186, 0.025864917, 0.025864923, 0.025864926, 0.025864952. The want 0.0258649 sits near the top of that band; the largest relative distance to any vintage is 2.8e-5, so RTOL 2.8e-5 admits every legal constant. The fixture uses 1e-4 - about 3.6x looser - while its header claims the tolerance is "wide enough to admit any of them - and nothing else". That last clause is what is unearned.
expected: Tighten the $vt RTOL to 3e-5, or re-centre the want on the band midpoint 0.02859457... (recompute) and tighten accordingly. Same argument applies to the 3e-3 on the diode current, which the header derives from an 8e-4 band.

title: Modulus by zero - the chapter's most explicit "shall be an error" - is not rejected anywhere
detail: VERIFIED. 4.2.4, verbatim: "It shall be an error to pass zero (0) as the second argument to the modulus operator." No fixture in ch04_expressions passes a zero second operand; 45_modulo.va uses 2.0 only. This is the single most quotable prohibition in the chapter.
expected: //! reject <code>\n//! lrm 4.2.4, on both `x % 0` (integer) and `x % 0.0` (real), since 4.2.1 admits % for real operands too.

title: "All other operators are considered illegal when used with real operands" has no rejecting fixture
detail: VERIFIED. 4.2.1: "The operators shown in Table 4-2 are legal when applied to real operands. All other operators are considered illegal when used with real operands." Table 4-2 admits unary +/-, + - * / **, %, relational, ==/!=, ! && ||, and ?:. Everything else - & | ^ ~ << >> and the reductions - is illegal on a real. src/diag_code.zig E0318 ("bitwise operator requires integer operands") exists but cites 4.2.9; nothing in the chapter exercises it against a real operand.
expected: //! reject E0318\n//! lrm 4.2.1, one file covering a bitwise and a shift applied to a real. Consider correcting E0318's cite from 4.2.9 to 4.2.1, which is where the rule actually lives.

title: "Input values outside of the valid range for the operator shall report an error" is never exercised
detail: VERIFIED. The sentence sits immediately above Table 4-15, whose Domain column is explicit: asin/acos want -1 <= x <= 1, atanh wants |x| < 1, acosh wants x >= 1, tan wants x != n(pi/2) for odd n. Nothing in the chapter calls any of them out of domain. 12_transcendental_math.va is deliberately built to stay inside every domain. Table 4-14 (4.3.1) has its own Domain column - ln and log10 want x > 0, sqrt wants x >= 0 - equally unexercised.
expected: One or two reject fixtures: `//! lrm 4.3.2` for asin(2.0)/acosh(0.5), and `//! lrm 4.3.1` for ln(-1.0)/sqrt(-1.0). Constant arguments so the check is static.

title: "A port access function can not be used on the left side of a branch assignment or contribution statement"
detail:
VERIFIED, verbatim from 4.4. 34_port_access.va exercises `I(

)` on the RIGHT of a contribution (`I(p) <+ I(

);`) and asserts its value, but the LHS prohibition - the sentence that distinguishes a port access from a branch access - is untested.
expected:
//! reject \n//! lrm 4.4 on `I(

) <+ 1.0;`.

title: "Unsized constant numbers shall not be allowed in concatenations" is not rejected
detail: VERIFIED, verbatim from 4.2.13. 30_concatenation.va uses only sized literals (4'b1010, 4'b0101). src/diag_code.zig already has E0216 "concatenation operand has no bit width" cited to 4.2.13, so the code exists and is simply unexercised from this chapter.

title: "expressions containing replications shall not appear on the left-hand side of an assignment"
detail: VERIFIED, verbatim from 4.2.13. src/diag_code.zig E0317 ("a concatenation is not an assignment target") already quotes this exact sentence in its explain text, so the diagnostic exists and the rule has no fixture. NOTE: blocked behind CH04-011 - VerA cannot currently parse a replication at all, so this fixture would pass for the wrong reason (a parse error, not the LHS rule). Sequence it after 31 is fixed, or pin E0317 explicitly rather than a phase label.
expected: //! reject E0317\n//! lrm 4.2.13 on `{2{a}} = b;`, written to fail on the LHS rule and not on the parse.

title: ddx()'s second argument must be an access function, and neither violation is rejected
detail: VERIFIED. 18_ddx.va calls ddx(expr, V(p)) and ddx(expr, V(n)) only. 4.5.6 constrains the second argument to be an access function of an unknown; a two-node potential V(p,n) and a plain variable are both outside it. Neither is rejected, and ddx with respect to a FLOW - I(...) - is not exercised on the positive side either (see CH04-039).
expected: //! reject <code>\n//! lrm 4.5.6, two cases in one file: `ddx(x, V(p,n))` and `ddx(x, y)` where y is a real variable.

title: The LEGAL side of 4.5.15's conditional rule has no fixture: a constant-condition guard must COMPILE
detail: VERIFIED. 4.5.15: "Analog operators shall not be used inside conditional (if, case, or ?:) statements UNLESS the conditional expression controlling the statement consists of terms which can not change their value during the course of a simulation." Every fixture in the family (36, 88-93) is a reject. Nothing pins the carve-out, so a compiler that rejects ALL conditional analog operators - over-strict, and a real and easy implementation mistake - passes the whole chapter clean.
expected: A running fixture: `//! lrm 4.5.15`, a parameter-guarded `if (use_filter) I(p,n) <+ transition(...)`, with a CHECKX on the DC value. This is the highest-value single item in the missing-coverage set because it is the only thing that can catch over-rejection.

title: 4.5.15 names if, case and ?:; only `if` is rejected. `always` is likewise uncovered
detail: VERIFIED. 4.5.15 lists "conditional (if, case, or ?:) statements"; 36_operator_in_conditional.va covers `if` only. Separately, "they can not be used inside an initial or always block" - 93_operator_in_initial.va covers `initial`; no ch04 fixture contains `always` (`always` IS a reserved word in src/frontend/token.zig, so the fixture is writable). 3 new reject files, all pinning E0514 or E0422.
expected: Three files: an analog operator under a non-constant `case`, under a non-constant `?:`, and inside an `always` block. `//! lrm 4.5.15` on each.

title: Five unenforced analog-operator argument constraints, one reject fixture each
detail: VERIFIED against 4.5.5-4.5.10 and against the fixtures, all of which use one well-formed argument list and never a bad one: idtmod's modulus "shall be an expression which evaluates to a positive value" (17_idtmod.va uses 2.0 only); absdelay's td must be positive (19 uses 2n only); transition's "td, rise_time, fall_time, and time_tol ... if specified shall be non-negative" (20 uses 1n,2n,3n only); slew's rising rate must be positive and falling negative (21 uses 1e6,-2e6 only); last_crossing's direction indicator must be in {+1,-1,0} (22 uses 1 only). 5 new .va files sharing one shape: a constant out-of-range argument, `//! reject`, `//! lrm`.
expected: Five reject fixtures with constant offending arguments so the check can be static. Expect `//! xfail` on most: no evidence VerA validates any of these bounds today.

title: Laplace unpaired complex root, Z-filter non-positive T, and the zero-transition branch ban
detail: VERIFIED verbatim in ch4-expressions.html: 4.5.11.1/4.5.12.1 "If a root is complex, its conjugate shall also be present"; 4.5.12 "T specifies the period of the filter, is mandatory, and shall be positive" and "tau ... shall be nonnegative" and "A Z-filter with zero (0) transition time shall not be directly assigned to a branch". 23_laplace_filters.va supplies a properly conjugate-paired pole vector and 24 supplies T=1u, so all three prohibitions are unexercised. 3 new reject files.
expected: Three reject fixtures: an unpaired complex Laplace root, `zi_zd(..., T)` with T = 0 or negative, and `I(p,n) <+ zi_zp(..., 1u, 0.0);` for the zero-tau branch ban. `//! lrm` on each.

title: "shall only be called within the analog context" is not rejected
detail: VERIFIED. 4.7.3 restricts calls on analog user-defined functions to the analog context. No ch04 fixture calls one from an initial block or a module-level continuous assignment. Related and also missing: 4.7.2.2's `return` with no expression or with the wrong type (40_function_return_rejected.va is an accept fixture and exercises neither).
expected: Two reject fixtures: an analog function called from an `initial` block (`//! lrm 4.7.3`), and a bare `return;` / type-mismatched return inside an analog function (`//! lrm 4.7.2.2`).

title: Three shape rules on the access-function argument list have no fixture
detail: VERIFIED. 4.4: "The argument expression list for signal access functions shall be a branch identifier, or a list of one or two nets or port expressions" and "The net identifiers shall be scalar or resolve to a constant net of a composite net type (array or bus) accessed by a genvar expression". Untested: three net arguments, a composite-net access indexed by a non-genvar expression, and a port access `<x>` whose operand is not a module port. NOTE the middle one is largely moot while src/diag_code.zig E0302 says vector nets are unsupported - it will reject for the wrong reason. Sequence it last or accept an xfail.
expected: Three small reject fixtures, `//! lrm 4.4` on each.

title: Three replication-constant rules unexercised; all blocked behind CH04-011
detail: VERIFIED in 4.2.13: a negative/x/z replication constant is illegal; "Such a replication shall appear only within a concatenation in which at least one of the operands of the concatenation has a positive size" (the LRM prints two illegal-for-P=32 examples); and a replication may not connect to an output or inout port. None has a fixture. All three are unreachable as written until VerA parses replications at all - CH04-011 must land first or these pass on a parse error.
expected: Three reject fixtures, `//! lrm 4.2.13`, explicitly pinning a semantic code rather than ParseError so they cannot pass for the parse-gap reason.

title: An array output/inout actual of the wrong size is not rejected
detail: PARTIALLY VERIFIED - the lens claimed "wrong size OR containing non-variables"; the non-variable half is ALREADY COVERED by 106_function_output_nonvariable.va and 107_function_inout_nonvariable.va, which pass branch probes and pin E0316, matching 4.7.2.3's own worked counter-example ("Only analog variable references can be passed to output and inout arguments"). Only the wrong-size half survives, and it is blocked behind CH04-007/008 for the same parse reason.
expected: One reject fixture passing a 3-element pattern to a [0:1] formal. `//! lrm 4.7.2.3`.

title: Three low-value prohibitions with no fixture
detail: VERIFIED as uncovered but low-yield: x or z bits converted to a real (4.2.1.2); an assignment pattern used in a context 4.2.14 does not list; a non-constant noise_table file name or duplicate frequencies in the table (4.6.4.3). Each is real, each is narrow, and none is likely to catch a live bug in a Verilog-A-only compiler.
expected: Three reject fixtures if the chapter is being taken to completeness. Skip them if it is not - say so in COVERAGE.md rather than leaving the rows blank.

title: 9 of Table 4-3's 13 precedence levels are untested, and the fixture cites the wrong table
detail: VERIFIED. Table 4-3 ("Precedence rules for operators") is in 4.2.2 and has 13 rows. 03_precedence_associativity.va pins exactly one adjacency - `/` above binary `+ -` - plus left-associativity of `+ -`; 01_arithmetic_operators.va adds `**` above unary above `* / %`. Everything from the shift row down is untested: << vs +-, relational vs shift, equality vs relational, & vs equality, ^ vs &, | vs ^, && vs |, || vs &&, ?: vs ||. Each is a distinct row boundary and each is where a precedence-climbing parser goes wrong. SEPARATELY: the fixture's header cites "LRM 4.2.9 Table 4-4" - 4.2.9 is Bitwise operators and Table 4-4 is "Arithmetic operators defined". Both citations are wrong.
expected: One all-integer fixture so every want is a CHECKI with no rounding, each literal chosen so an adjacent-swap or flat left-to-right parse yields a different number: `1 << 2 + 3` == 32 (flat gives 7), `1 << 2 < 8` == 1, `1 & 2 == 2` == 1, and so on down the table. Fix the citation to 4.2.2 / Table 4-3.

title: Short-circuit evaluation and its side-effect suppression have zero coverage
detail: VERIFIED. COVERAGE.md line 12 credits `04_relational_logical.va` for 4.2.3 - that fixture uses && and || but contains no function call, no assignment inside an operand, and therefore nothing whose suppression is observable. COVERAGE.md is at least honest about the residue ("suppression of runtime side effects requires numeric execution"), but the row reads as covered. A compiler that evaluates both operands of && passes every fixture in the chapter.
expected: A running fixture whose right operand has an observable effect - an analog function that increments an inout counter - asserting the counter is NOT bumped when the left operand of && is false, and IS bumped when it is true. Two CHECKI wants. Update the COVERAGE.md row at the same time.

title: >> is never applied to a negative operand, so an arithmetic-shift lowering passes
detail: VERIFIED. 4.2.11: "Both the << and >> shift operators fill the vacated bit positions with zeroes (0)", and 3.2 fixes integer at 32 bits two's-complement. 61_shift_right.va tests only 8>>2 and 3>>1, both non-negative, where a logical and an arithmetic shift agree. With -8 (0xFFFFFFF8), `-8 >> 1` must be 0x7FFFFFFC = 2147483644; a compiler that lowered >> to an arithmetic shift yields -4 and passes the chapter as it stands. This is the cheapest high-value want in the audit: one CHECKI line.
expected: Add `CHECKI("-8 >> 1 zero-fills, it does not sign-extend", (-8) >> 1, 2147483644);` to 61_shift_right.va, with the 32-bit derivation in the header. Consider the matching `<<` overflow case in 60.

title: "If a root is zero, then the term associated with it is implemented as s" - the one case that divides by zero - is untested
detail: VERIFIED. 4.5.11.1, verbatim: "If a root is zero (0), then the term associated with it is implemented as s, rather than (1 - s/r) (where r is the root)." 23_laplace_filters.va passes zeros `'{-1.0, 0.0}` - which is ONE root at -1+0j, a real root at minus one, not a root at the origin. So the special case that exists precisely because (1 - s/0) divides by zero is never entered. The identical rule in 4.5.12.1 IS reached by 24, whose header says so.
expected: Add a laplace_zp call with a root AT the origin - zeros `'{0.0, 0.0}` - and pin its DC gain. With the zero term implemented as s, H(0) = 0; a naive (1 - s/r) lowering produces inf or NaN, which is exactly the failure the sentence guards.

title: Output-reset-to-zero vs inout-left-untouched - the only observable difference between the two directions - is untested
detail: VERIFIED. 39_function_output_inout.va assigns result_area, result_perimeter AND accumulator inside the function, so every copy-out path is taken and the two directions behave identically. 4.7.2.3 says an output argument is initialized and "the argument passed to it is reset to zero" if unassigned; 4.7.2.4 says an unassigned inout leaves "the analog variable reference ... left untouched". Those two sentences are the entire semantic difference between output and inout, and nothing exercises either.
expected: One running fixture: a function that assigns NEITHER its output nor its inout formal, called with both actuals pre-set to a non-zero value. CHECKX the output actual to 0.0 and the inout actual to its pre-set value. A compiler that treats the two directions alike fails exactly one of the two.

title: None of Table 4-6's five worked rows is pinned
detail: VERIFIED - and the uncovered lens UNDERSTATED this. Table 4-6 has five rows: 11%3=2, 12%3=0, -10%3=-1, 11%-3=2, 10%3.75=2.5. 45_modulo.va pins neither of the integer sign cases nor the real example, only 5.5%2.0 and (-5.5)%2.0 from a bias. The LRM hands over five free literals - including 11%-3=2, the row that pins "the result takes the sign of the FIRST operand" against the common wrong answer -1 - and the fixture uses none of them.
expected: Add all five Table 4-6 rows as CHECKI/CHECKX wants, keeping the existing bias-derived pair. 11%-3 == 2 is the load-bearing one.

title: "if unspecified, the default is real" - every function fixture writes the type explicitly
detail: VERIFIED by grepping every `analog function` declaration in the chapter: all sixteen read `analog function real <name>`. 4.7.1's "type can be real, integer, or string; if unspecified, the default is real" is therefore untested in all three of its clauses - the implicit default, the `integer` form and the `string` form.
expected: A running fixture declaring `analog function untyped_ret;` with no type and pinning a real-valued result; optionally a second with an explicit `integer` return exercising 4.2.1.1 truncation.

title: Every stateful-operator fixture uses exactly one argument-list shape; all the optional and default forms are unwritten
detail: VERIFIED one file at a time. 17 always writes idtmod(x, ic, modulus, offset) - the three stated defaults are unexercised. 18 uses ddx w.r.t. a potential only - never a FLOW. 19 always writes absdelay(x, 2n) - `maxdelay` does not appear anywhere in tests/fixtures (grepped tree-wide, zero hits). 20 always writes the 4-argument transition - so "if only a positive rise_time value is specified, the simulator uses it for both rise and fall times" is untested. 21 always writes slew(x, 1e6, -2e6) - the 1-argument and 2-argument forms are unwritten. 22 queries direction +1 only - directions 0 and -1 never. Six edits, each adding calls in the omitted shapes with DC-derivable wants.
expected: Extend each fixture with its omitted argument shapes rather than adding six new files - the DC value is already derived in each header, so the incremental want is cheap.

title: The `,,` null zeros argument is legal for both Laplace and Z filters and appears nowhere in the tree
detail: VERIFIED. Both 4.5.11 and 4.5.12 carry the identical sentence: "The zeros argument may be represented as a null argument. The null argument is characterized by two adjacent commas (,,) in the argument list." A tree-wide grep for `,,` in *.va returns nothing. NOTE src/diag_code.zig E0505 is "analog operator does not accept an empty argument" (4.5.14) - so VerA may currently reject the legal form, in which case this lands with an //! xfail and doubles as evidence that E0505 is over-firing.
expected: A running fixture calling laplace_zp(x,,poles) and zi_zp(x,,poles,T) with DC gains derived from the poles alone.

title: The replication form of the assignment pattern, '{5{0.0}}, is nowhere in the tree
detail: VERIFIED. 4.2.14 prints the example itself: "parameter real data2[0:4] = '{ 5{0.0} };" with the explanation "The example also uses a replication operator to repeat 0.0 five times so that every element of data2 is assigned to 0.0." A tree-wide grep for `'{5{` returns nothing; 09_assignment_pattern.va uses only the enumerated form '{3.4, 5.6, 2.3, 4.5, 7.1}.
expected: Add the LRM's own `'{ 5{0.0} }` initializer to 09 and CHECKX two elements. Distinct from CH04-011: this is the assignment-pattern replication, not the concatenation replication.

title: Only the DC column of Table 4-22 is ever queried
detail: VERIFIED. 26_analysis.va runs under a DC operating point and asserts analysis("tran"), analysis("ac") and analysis("noise") are all 0 - it never runs an analysis in which any of them is 1. So a compiler that hardwired analysis() to return 1 for "dc"/"static" and 0 for everything else passes the chapter. `//! analysis tran` is a working directive (26 files across ch05, ch09, ch10 use it), so the fixture is writable today. Unsupported analysis names are also untested.
expected: A sibling fixture under `//! analysis tran` asserting analysis("tran")==1 and analysis("dc")==0 - the mirror image of 26 - which together pin two columns of Table 4-22.

title: 40 quotes "return shall OVERRIDE any value assigned to the function name" and never assigns the function name
detail: VERIFIED. `choose` uses `return` only; its identifier variable is never written, so there is nothing for the return to override and the fixture cannot distinguish the override rule from "return works". Also unexercised: 4.7.2.1's "If this internal variable is not assigned ... the function will return the variable's default initial value" (zero for a numeric type). The filename says `_rejected` on what is an accept fixture - the header already apologises for it.
expected: Assign the function name to a distinctly wrong value BEFORE the return, so the want can only be produced by the override. Add a second function that assigns nothing at all and pin its result to 0.0 for 4.7.2.1. Rename the file 40_function_return.va.

title: noise_table's and noise_table_log's interpolation rules are written out in the LRM and pinned by nothing
detail: VERIFIED. 27_noise_sources.va is the only noise_table user in the chapter. 4.6.4.3 states the piecewise-linear interpolation, the sorting requirement and the out-of-range clamping; 4.6.4.4 writes out the log-log interpolation formula explicitly. A formula printed in the LRM is a literal oracle, and neither is used.
expected: A running fixture per section evaluating the stated formula at a frequency strictly between two table points, plus a point below the first and above the last for the clamping rule.

title: "true (any value other than zero)" - a non-boolean ?: condition is never exercised
detail: VERIFIED. 4.2.12: "If expression1 evaluates to true (any value other than zero (0)), then expression2 is evaluated". 08_conditional_operator.va uses `V(p,n) > 1.0` and `V(p,n) < -1.0` - both relational, both already 0 or 1. A compiler that tested `cond == 1` instead of `cond != 0` passes.
expected: Add one line with a non-boolean condition - `2.5 ? a : b` or an integer 7 - and pin the true arm.

title: Table 4-20's constant/dynamic argument split, and 4.5.15's "no state history prior to t == 0", have no fixture
detail: VERIFIED. Table 4-20 ("Analog operator arguments") partitions each operator's arguments into constant-expression and dynamic-expression columns; no fixture in the chapter freezes a dynamic argument or feeds a non-constant expression to a constant slot. 4.5.15's "All analog operators are considered to have no state history prior to time t == 0" is likewise unpinned - and it is the sentence that would settle CH04-012.
expected: Two items, both low urgency: a reject fixture feeding a probe to a Table 4-20 constant slot, and a `//! time 0, ...` fixture asserting an operator's value at t == 0 against the no-history rule.

title: The abstol and nature forms of ddt and idt are never written
detail: VERIFIED. 14_ddt.va uses the one-argument ddt only; 15_idt.va does not reach the four- or five-argument forms. 4.5.3 defines ddt(expr, abstol) and ddt(expr, nature); 4.5.4 the corresponding idt forms. Low value in a DC-only harness - the tolerance argument has no observable effect on the operating point - but the SHAPES should at least parse.
expected: Add the extra-argument call shapes to 14 and 15 with the same DC wants; the claim is that they compile and agree, which is a CHECKEQ.

title: Port access on a bus port element, I(<p[i]>), is not exercised
detail: VERIFIED as uncovered, but BLOCKED: src/diag_code.zig E0301 is "vector ports are not supported" (6.5.2), so this fixture can only land as an //! xfail and will reject for the vector-port reason rather than testing anything about 4.4. Lowest value item in the set.
expected: Defer. If written, `//! lrm 4.4` + `//! xfail vector ports unsupported (E0301)`.

title: Not one fixture in the chapter carries a //! lrm cite
detail: VERIFIED by grep: `grep -l '^//! lrm' *.va` returns zero of 118 files, while 26 carry `//! reject`. tests/torture.zig documents //! lrm as the mechanism behind `zig build torture -- --coverage`, which "prints every cited section, sorted, with the fixtures citing it" - described in README as "the only mechanical backing a 'chapter 4 is covered' claim can have". With zero cites, ch04's coverage claim has no mechanical backing at all, and a failing fixture cannot report which rule broke. Every fixture already names its section in a header comment, so this is a mechanical lift.
expected: Add one or more `//! lrm <section>` lines to every fixture, taken from the section already quoted in its header. Do this LAST, after the rewrites above settle which rule each file actually pins - several currently cite the wrong one (see CH04-032, CH04-050, CH04-052).

title: 24 stale sidecar files remain despite README's "No sidecar files"
detail: VERIFIED, with two lens claims CORRECTED. There are 24 sidecars, not the 21 the negatives lens reported. All 24 agree EXACTLY with their fixture's in-file `//! reject` - I diffed every pair - so the negatives lens's claim that "05's sidecar contradicts its own in-file //! reject E0324" is FALSE (both read E0324), and the weak lens's "the two copies already disagree" is false on content. They disagree only in COUNT: 26 reject fixtures, 24 sidecars, with 104 and 105 missing theirs. tests/conformance.zig, the only reader of these files, is not wired into build.zig - the sole fixture step is `torture`. So they are dead weight that README already forbids.
expected: Delete all 24 `.expected-error.txt` files. Consider deleting tests/conformance.zig with them, or wiring it up - as it stands it is an unrun second oracle.

title: 93 and 94 expect the bare phase label DiagnosticsReported, which ANY diagnostic satisfies
detail: VERIFIED. Both files' only expectation is `//! reject DiagnosticsReported` - satisfied by a typo, a missing include, or any unrelated error, so neither pins its rule. README is explicit that "Codes are the preferred form ... they pin WHICH rule fired rather than how it happened to be worded." The right codes already exist in src/diag_code.zig: E0422 "analog operator is not allowed in this context" (lrm 4.5.15) for 93, and E0505 "analog operator does not accept an empty argument" (lrm 4.5.14) for 94.
expected: Change 93 to `//! reject E0422` and 94 to `//! reject E0505`, each with the matching `//! lrm`.

title: 102 pins E0511 "wrong number of arguments", not the direction rule it claims to test
detail: VERIFIED. src/diag_code.zig E0511 is titled "wrong number of arguments to an analog function" (lrm 4.7.2). 102 declares `analog function real undirected; real x; undirected=x;` - with no direction, `x` is a local, so the function has ZERO formals and the call `undirected(V(p))` passes one actual. E0511 fires on the ARITY. The 4.7.1 rule the header cites ("all formal arguments shall have an associated direction specification") is never reached, and the fixture would pass unchanged if the direction rule were deleted from the compiler.
expected: Either add a new code for the missing-direction rule and pin it, or rewrite the fixture so the arity matches and only the direction is wrong. Same class of defect as CH04-053.

title: Two reject fixtures pin the right verdict via the wrong rule
detail: VERIFIED. 103 pins `E0314` ("unknown identifier", lrm 6.8) plus the bare substring `outer` for what 4.7.1 states as "shall only reference locally-defined variables, variables passed as arguments, locally-defined parameters and module-level parameters" - a scope-lookup failure standing in for a normative restriction. 05_bitwise_shift.va cites "LRM 4.2.9" in both its header and its sidecar for the sentence "The arithmetic shift operators can not be used in an analog block", which is in 4.2.11 - 4.2.9 is Bitwise operators. 05 also folds nine legal operators into the one rejected expression, so it cannot say which token drew the diagnostic.
expected: Fix 05's citation to 4.2.11 and reduce its expression to the single `>>>` (and a sibling for `<<<`). For 103, either accept E0314 and correct the header's claim, or add a 4.7.1-specific code.

title: Three fixtures assert relational claims through CHECK/CHECKI instead of CHECKEQ
detail: VERIFIED. 21 line 35: `CHECKI("never overshoots its input", slew(V(p,n),1e6,-2e6) <= V(p,n), 1)`. 19 line 37 is the same shape. 17 line 30 is `CHECKI(..., (idtmod(...) >= 0.0) && (idtmod(...) < 2.0), 1)`, and 17/19/21 each also use `operator(...) - closed_form` against 0.0. These are inequalities and identities dressed as value assertions: an error common to both sides passes them, and a range check passes for any value in the range. README reserves CHECKEQ for exactly this weaker class "so the weaker claims stay greppable".
expected: Move the identity forms to CHECKEQ. Keep the range/inequality checks but stop counting them as pinned values - each of these three fixtures should also carry at least one real literal want.

title: 104/105 demand E0510 while COVERAGE.md says the recursion check is missing
detail: PARTIALLY VERIFIED - one lens claim CORRECTED. Both files carry `//! reject E0510` and are the only two rejects in the chapter with no sidecar. src/diag_code.zig DOES define E0510 ("recursive analog function", lrm 4.7.1) with a full explain, but COVERAGE.md line 62 says the two fixtures "retain direct and mutual recursive definitions without executing them, pinning the MISSING static recursion check". Both cannot be true. The weak lens's framing - that conformance.zig and torture.zig "currently demand opposite things" - is FALSE: conformance.zig has no build step in build.zig, so only torture runs. The live contradiction is between the fixtures and COVERAGE.md, not between two runners.
expected: Run `zig build torture -- ch04` and settle it: if E0510 fires, fix the COVERAGE.md sentence; if it does not, add `//! xfail`. Also note 104/105 cite 4.7.3 in their headers while E0510 records lrm 4.7.1.

title: COVERAGE.md justifies nine fixtures with "snapshots current behavior" and credits rules no fixture reaches
detail: VERIFIED line by line. Five rows use snapshot language - 4.2.13 "snapshots current brace lowering", 4.6.3 "snapshots current generic-call behavior", 4.6.4.6 "snapshots current sharing/dataflow behavior", 4.7.2.2 "snapshots current acceptance", plus line 62's "pin the current acceptance gap" covering four more files. That is the recorded-transcript oracle README says this suite exists to replace. Separately, line 12 credits 04_relational_logical.va for 4.2.3 short-circuit (see CH04-033), and line 25 credits 86 and 87 to 4.4 while noting "Both currently compile and therefore pin semantic-validation gaps" - describing an inverted fixture as coverage.
expected: Rewrite every snapshot row to state the RULE and the fixture's status against it (covered / xfail / uncovered). Do this after the tier-1 rewrites, since eleven of the rows change meaning. Add rows for the sections CH04-016 through CH04-048 leave open.
